# spec


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A freezer needs to be told what goes into an app: the script to run, the
packages to copy, the modules it would miss, the data files, the icon,
and the metadata macOS reads from the bundle’s `Info.plist`. py2app and
py2exe each take this as a dictionary of options, and they name the
options differently. This module lets you write the description once, as
an [`App`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/spec.html#app), and
produces either dictionary from it.

### tree

``` python
def tree(
    src, dest, skip:tuple=()
):
```

*List every file under `src` as the `(dest_dir, [files])` pairs a
freezer takes, with `src` mapped to `dest`.*

Data files are files the app reads at run time that are not Python code,
such as CSS, JavaScript and images. A freezer takes them as a list of
`(dest_dir, [files])` pairs, where `dest_dir` is a folder inside the
bundle and `files` are paths on your disk.
[`tree`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/spec.html#tree) builds
that list for a whole folder. It walks `src`, mirrors its layout under
`dest`, skips hidden files, `__pycache__` and any folder named in
`skip`, and sorts the pairs so that two builds produce the same list.
Pass the result as `App(data=...)`. The example skips `node_modules` and
the hidden `.DS_Store`.

``` python
data = tree(src, 'demo/static', skip=['node_modules'])
[(dest, [Path(f).name for f in files]) for dest, files in data]
```

    [('demo/static', ['app.css']),
     ('demo/static/img', ['logo.png']),
     ('demo/static/js', ['app.js'])]

Some packages ship parts compiled with mypyc, and the compiled parts
load a helper extension module whose file name contains `__mypyc`.
Nothing imports that helper by name, so a freezer that follows `import`
statements leaves it out and the app fails when it starts.
[`mypyc_modules`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/spec.html#mypyc_modules)
lists these helpers in the `site-packages` of the environment you build
from, or in the folder `site`. Add the result to `App(includes=...)`.
The helpers’ file names include the Python version and platform, which
is why they are looked up at build time instead of written into the spec
by hand.

``` python
site = Path(tmp.name)/'site'; site.mkdir()
for f in ('chardet__mypyc.cpython-313-darwin.so', 'numpy.cpython-313-darwin.so'): (site/f).write_text('')
mypyc_modules(site)
```

    ['chardet__mypyc']

A freezer also pulls in modules no app needs, because something in the
environment mentions them. `DEFAULT_EXCLUDES` lists the usual ones:
build tools such as setuptools and the freezers themselves, the standard
library’s test suite, other GUI toolkits, and matplotlib. `GUI_MODULE`
names pywebview’s module for each platform, so that a build can leave
out the two it does not use.

### App

``` python
def App(
    name:str, entry:str, version:str='0.0.0', build:str='', icon:str='', modern_icon:str='', identifier:str='',
    summary:str='', packages:list=<factory>, includes:list=<factory>, excludes:list=<factory>,
    grafted:list=<factory>, unreachable:list=<factory>, data:list=<factory>, plist:dict=<factory>,
    doc_types:list=<factory>, extras:list=<factory>, min_macos:str='11.0',
    category:str='public.app-category.developer-tools'
)->None:
```

*Describe an app once, for whichever freezer this platform uses.*

[`App`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/spec.html#app) is the
description itself. Only `name` and `entry`, the script the app runs,
are required; the comment beside each field says what it holds. If you
leave out `identifier`, the reverse-DNS name macOS uses to tell apps
apart, it becomes `org.<name>.<name>` in lower case. `bundle_name` is
the name the freezer gives its output, `Demo.app` on macOS and `Demo`
elsewhere, and `out(root)` is where that ends up, under `root/dist`. The
saved output below came from a machine that is not a Mac, so it shows
`Demo`.

``` python
app = App(name='Demo', entry='demo_app.py', version='1.2.3', summary='the demo app',
          icon='assets/Demo.icns', packages=['demo', 'fasthtml', 'uvicorn'],
          includes=['demo.cli'], data=data, extras=['desktop'])
app.identifier, app.bundle_name, str(app.out('/build/demo'))
```

    ('org.demo.demo', 'Demo', '/build/demo/dist/Demo')

``` python
app.info_plist()
```

    {'CFBundleName': 'Demo',
     'CFBundleDisplayName': 'Demo',
     'CFBundleIdentifier': 'org.demo.demo',
     'CFBundleVersion': '1.2.3',
     'CFBundleShortVersionString': '1.2.3',
     'CFBundleGetInfoString': 'the demo app',
     'LSApplicationCategoryType': 'public.app-category.developer-tools',
     'LSMinimumSystemVersion': '11.0',
     'NSHighResolutionCapable': True,
     'NSRequiresAquaSystemAppearance': False,
     'NSAppTransportSecurity': {'NSAllowsLocalNetworking': True},
     'LSEnvironment': {'LANG': 'en_US.UTF-8', 'PYTHONUTF8': '1'}}

`CFBundleVersion` is what Launch Services compares when several copies
of one app are registered, so local builds that all carry the same
`version` leave it picking an arbitrary copy. Setting `App.build` to a
value that grows with every build, such as `1.2.3.29600000`, makes the
newest copy win. `CFBundleShortVersionString` stays the `version`, and
with no
[`build`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/build.html#build) both
entries are the `version`.

``` python
test_eq(App('Demo', 'd.py', version='1.2.3').info_plist()['CFBundleVersion'], '1.2.3')
built = App('Demo', 'd.py', version='1.2.3', build='1.2.3.29600000').info_plist()
test_eq((built['CFBundleVersion'], built['CFBundleShortVersionString']), ('1.2.3.29600000', '1.2.3'))
built['CFBundleVersion']
```

`info_plist` returns the entries for `Info.plist`, the file macOS reads
to learn an app’s name, version and abilities. Three of the defaults
matter for a web app in a window. `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` lets the
window load pages from the local server over plain HTTP.
`NSRequiresAquaSystemAppearance` set to `False` lets the app follow dark
mode. `LSEnvironment` sets `PYTHONUTF8` and `LANG` so that Python starts
in UTF-8. Any entry in `App.plist` overrides the default of the same
name.

``` python
app.py2app_options()['excludes']
```

    ['PyQt5',
     'PyQt6',
     'PySide2',
     'PySide6',
     'clr',
     'gi',
     'matplotlib',
     'py2app',
     'py2exe',
     'setuptools',
     'test',
     'tkinter',
     'webview.platforms.gtk',
     'webview.platforms.winforms',
     'wheel']

`excluded` combines `DEFAULT_EXCLUDES`, the app’s own `excludes` and the
pywebview modules for the other platforms, with no duplicates.
`py2app_options` and `py2exe_options` each call it for their own
platform. The list above is the macOS one, so it leaves out the GTK and
WinForms modules and keeps Cocoa.

``` python
o = app.py2app_options()
o['packages'].append('scipy')
test_eq(app.packages, ['demo', 'fasthtml', 'uvicorn'])
noisy = App(name='D', entry='e.py', excludes=['mlx', 'mlx', 'tkinter']).excluded('darwin')
test_eq(noisy.count('tkinter'), 1)
test_eq(noisy, sorted(set(noisy)))
```

### doc_types

``` python
def doc_types(
    extensions, view_elsewhere:tuple=('.svg', '.html', '.htm', '.pdf')
):
```

*Build the `Info.plist` document types that let Finder open folders, and
files with these `extensions`, in the app.*

An app can tell macOS which files it opens, so that Finder lists it
under Open With and lets the user drop files on its icon. These
declarations go in `Info.plist` under `CFBundleDocumentTypes`.
[`doc_types`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/spec.html#doc_types)
writes two of them. The first covers folders, with the rank `Alternate`,
so the app is offered for a folder without replacing Finder as the
default. The second makes the app the `Owner`, the default editor, of
every extension you pass. Extensions a browser shows better, by default
`.svg`, `.html`, `.htm` and `.pdf`, are left out, and the leading dot is
optional. Pass the result as `App(doc_types=...)`.

``` python
folder, files = doc_types(['.py', 'py', '.rs', '.svg', '.pdf'])
files['CFBundleTypeExtensions'], folder['LSHandlerRank'], files['LSHandlerRank']
```

    (['py', 'rs'], 'Alternate', 'Owner')

``` python
test_eq(files['CFBundleTypeExtensions'], ['py', 'rs'])
test_eq(folder['LSItemContentTypes'], ['public.folder'])
```
